unlisted_practices: Government bodies should invest in infrastructure to support the safe, effective, and equitable use of AI in healthcare.
Healthcare delivery organizations and AI frameworks should prioritize environmental sustainability in AI use, including careful selection of AI technologies to reduce greenhouse gas emissions.

Payers and policymakers should develop mature reimbursement mechanisms that support responsible AI use, such as value- and outcome-based reimbursement, advance market commitments, time-limited reimbursement for new products, and financial incentives for bias mitigation.
AI frameworks and best-practice guides should more prominently prioritize beneficence and the impact of AI on people's well-being.
Best practices should be strengthened to improve the experience of workers who increasingly interact with AI and to address workforce displacement.
AI frameworks should more rigorously consider whether AI is applied to appropriate problems and the conditions under which AI solutions are updated and decommissioned.
AI frameworks should address sociotechnical challenges at the interface of human users and AI technologies, including clinician workflow design and testing.

screen.reason: This paper presents a framework/mapping of AI principles and regulatory frameworks to best practice guides for healthcare delivery organizations, representing guidelines/commentary rather than an empirical evaluation.
